title: Repo Health Doctor: issues, empty CLAUDE.md sections, unanswered comments
desc: Periodic repo health check covering GitHub issues (close Daily reports, triage real bugs), unanswered issue comments, empty CLAUDE.md sections (Gotchas/Skills stubs), and launch checklist progress comments. Run before release or when repo feels stale.
steps: WHEN TO RUN: before a release, after a sprint, or when repo feels stale. Also triggered from claude-md-guide situation H (periodic check).

STEP 1 -- GitHub issues: gh issue list --state open. (A) [Daily] WKAppBot Report entries -> close all: gh issue close <n> --reason completed --comment "Closing automated daily report". (B) Real bugs -> check if fixed in recent commits: git log --oneline --since=<issue-date>
grep -i <keyword>. If fixed -> close with version. If not -> comment with current status. (C) Feature requests -> comment with roadmap note or file suggest: wkappbot suggest "title".

STEP 2 -- Unanswered issue comments: for each open issue with comments, run gh issue view <n> --comments. Look for questions or requests from external contributors that have no owner reply. Draft a reply and post: gh issue comment <n> --body "...".

STEP 3 -- CLAUDE.md empty sections: Read project CLAUDE.md. Find stub lines: '- (add project-specific gotchas here)', '# Remove keywords that don't apply', empty ## Skills or ## Gotchas. Actions: (A) Skills stub -> run the search line, pick top 3 relevant skills, replace stub with actual reads. (B) Gotchas stub -> scan recent git log and suggest list for lessons learned, fill in real gotchas. (C) Build section missing -> add from actual dotnet publish / npm run / make command.

STEP 4 -- Launch checklist (if issue #1 exists in repo): gh issue view 1 --comments. Check latest progress comment. If new items were completed since last comment, post an update: list completed items, update progress %, list remaining. Template: '### v<X.Y.Z> release -- <date>' + completed items + current progress + remaining table.
STEP 5 -- Commit any CLAUDE.md changes: git add CLAUDE.md && git commit -m 'docs: heal CLAUDE.md empty sections'. Push. Then run wkappbot skill read claude-md-guide to verify no drift with README.md.

README.md sync check: compare README.md against CLAUDE.md and recent commits. (A) Version number in README -> update to current (wkappbot --version). (B) Feature list / architecture section -> verify reflects latest changes from git log --oneline -20. (C) Quick-start commands -> run each one and confirm they still work. (D) Any section that overlaps with CLAUDE.md -> must agree exactly. If drift found: fix both in one commit. Rule: README is the public face -- if a user reads only README, they must get accurate current info.

AGENTS.md / CLAUDE.md parity (juniors forget this): if both exist, they must agree on shared AI policy -- delegation rules, language, notification method, process kill protection. Run: diff <(grep -A3 '##' CLAUDE.md) <(grep -A3 '##' AGENTS.md) as a sanity check. Any section present in one but absent in the other = drift. Fix in one commit. Codex reads AGENTS.md; Claude reads CLAUDE.md -- if they diverge, the two AIs work with different rules on the same repo.

Skill source_refs audit (juniors forget after refactors): wkappbot skill audit -- finds skills whose source_refs point to moved/renamed/deleted code. Stale refs waste future sessions (Claude reads the skill, tries the ref, gets confused). Fix: wkappbot skill edit <id> --source-refs updated-path. Do this after every file rename or module split.

gg section smoke test (user experience gate): actually send 'gg' and verify every step in ## gg Main Workflow runs without error. Common failures: (A) skill ID renamed -> update the read command. (B) suggest list times out -> add --timeout. (C) build command path changed -> fix inline. (D) Agent prompt references removed features -> update. If any step fails silently, the user gets no feedback and thinks gg worked. Fix before committing.

CI health check: gh run list --limit 5 -- verify latest runs are green. If red: gh run view <id> --log-failed to diagnose. Fix before release. Common CI failures after SDK work: path changes in scripts, new env var not set in secrets, binary size limit exceeded. Never ship a release with a red CI -- users see it on the badge and lose trust immediately.

Resolved suggests cleanup (SDK growth habit): wkappbot suggest list -- look for HALF state items (1-of-2 resolved) that are actually done. Run wkappbot suggest check <ts> --confirm to complete them. Also look for suggests that describe bugs already fixed in recent commits: close with wkappbot suggest resolve <ts> 'fixed in v<X.Y>'. Stale suggests mislead future sessions into thinking the bug is still open.

User-facing text audit (user experience): search for debug noise left in production -- grep -r 'Console.Error.Write.*\[DBG\]\|TODO\|FIXME\|HACK\|TEMP\b' csharp/src/ --include=*.cs. Also check --help output: wkappbot --help | grep -E '^\s+\w' -- every listed command should still exist and work. Remove or fix anything that would confuse a first-time user. First impressions matter: a user who hits a broken --help or debug spam in production will file an issue immediately.
